items.title: Ukraine marks four years since Russia's full-scale invasion amid fresh strikes

featured_image.name: Nationwide events mark fourth anniversary of Russia’s Ukraine invasion

items.description:
As February 24 arrives, marking the fourth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion, Ukraine and its global diaspora are pausing to mourn the dead, honor the displaced, and call on the world not to look away from Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II.

The anniversary comes days after Russia launched a massive combined missile and drone attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. On February 22, the Ukrainian Air Force reported that Russia fired 50 missiles and 297 drones targeting power facilities in Kyiv, Odesa, and central Ukraine, killing at least one person in the capital and leaving six regions without electricity. President Volodymyr Zelensky said on X that in just one week, Russia had unleashed over 1,000 drones, more than 1,400 guided bombs, and 96 missiles. "Moscow continues to prioritize military actions over diplomatic efforts," he wrote.[1][2]

items.title: Stock futures slide as Trump raises global tariffs to 15%

featured_image.name: Tariff ruling live coverage: Trump attacks Supreme Court, imposes 10% 'global tariff', then raises it to 15%

items.description:
U.S. stock futures slipped on Sunday evening as investors weighed the fallout from a turbulent 48 hours in trade policy. President Donald Trump's decision to raise a new global tariff to 15% — the maximum allowed under the legal authority he invoked — rattled markets just two days after the Supreme Court struck down the bulk of his original tariff regime.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futures fell roughly 0.4%, while S&P 500 futures dropped about 0.5% and Nasdaq-100 futures declined approximately 0.7%, according to MarketWatch.[1][2]

items.title: Trump weighs broader Iran military action, including targeting Khamenei

featured_image.name: Iran says US risking ‘crisis’ as Trump sets ’10, 15 days’ deadline for deal

items.description:
President Donald Trump has told his advisers that if diplomatic efforts or an initial targeted strike fail to compel Iran to abandon its nuclear ambitions, he may authorize a broader military operation in the coming months — one that could include an attempt to remove Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei from power, according to the New York Times, citing individuals familiar with internal discussions.[1]

The revelation comes as U.S. and Iranian negotiators prepare to meet in Geneva on Thursday in what appears to be a last-ditch round of talks, with two aircraft carrier strike groups now positioned within striking distance of Iran.[2][1]

items.title: Pentagon presented Trump with plan to target Iran's Khamenei, reports say

featured_image.name: Trump says he's considering limited military strike against Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump acknowledged on Friday that he is considering a limited military strike against Iran, even as the Pentagon has presented him with a range of scenarios that include options for targeting Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and his son Mojtaba, according to multiple reports citing senior administration officials.

"The most I can say — I am considering it," Trump told reporters at a White House breakfast with U.S. governors when asked about a potential limited strike if Iran fails to reach a deal over its nuclear program.[1][2][3]

items.title: Khamenei activates succession plan amid US strike threats, Times reports

featured_image.name: Ali Khamenei appoints succesor in event of US assassination

items.description:
The Pentagon has presented President Trump with military contingency plans that include a scenario to kill Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his son Mojtaba, Axios reported Friday, a disclosure that has prompted Iran's top leader to activate emergency succession frameworks as the two nations edge closer to a potential armed confrontation.

"They have something for every scenario. One scenario takes out the ayatollah and his son and the mullahs," a senior Trump adviser told Axios, referring to Khamenei and Mojtaba, who is widely viewed as a likely successor. A second source confirmed the plan was floated to Trump several weeks ago. The adviser added: "What the president chooses no one knows. I don't think he knows."[1][2]

White House spokesperson Anna Kelly declined to discuss specific military plans, saying "only President Trump knows what actions he may or may not take."[2][1]

items.title: Oman confirms US-Iran nuclear talks set for Thursday in Geneva

featured_image.name: Iran's Araghchi arrives in Geneva for second round of nuclear talks with US

items.description:
The United States and Iran are preparing for a third round of indirect nuclear negotiations in Geneva this week, as both sides signal a willingness to keep talking even as President Donald Trump weighs military action against Tehran.

Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi confirmed on Sunday that the talks are scheduled for Thursday, describing the upcoming session as proceeding "with a positive push to go the extra mile towards finalising the deal." Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, appearing on CBS News' "Face the Nation" the same day, said he expects to meet US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in Geneva on Thursday, adding, "I believe that still, there is a good chance to have a diplomatic solution which is based on a win-win game."[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Mexican army kills 'El Mencho,' leader of Jalisco cartel

featured_image.name: Leader of Mexico's Jalisco Cartel Reported Slain in Federal Raid

items.description:
The Mexican army killed Nemesio Rubén Oseguera Cervantes, the elusive leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel known as "El Mencho," during a military operation on Sunday in the western state of Jalisco, a federal official told the Associated Press. The death of one of the world's most wanted drug lords triggered a violent response from the cartel, with burning vehicles and roadblocks erupting across at least six Mexican states.[1][2]

The operation, carried out by special forces of the Mexican army and National Guard, took place in the mountainous area near Tapalpa in southern Jalisco, according to multiple Mexican media reports citing federal sources. El Mencho had long been reported to suffer from chronic kidney failure, which limited his mobility and forced him to rely on clandestine medical care in rural communities of Jalisco.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Trump says US will send hospital ship to Greenland

featured_image.name: Hospital Ship USNS Comfort Departs on Humanitarian Mission

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that the United States would send a "great hospital boat" to Greenland, claiming residents of the Arctic territory are "sick and not being taken care of." Denmark swiftly dismissed the plan, with the defense minister stating the self-governing territory's population already receives adequate healthcare.

Trump's announcement, made on Truth Social alongside an image of the USNS Mercy, a 1,000-bed naval hospital ship, came on the same day Danish military forces evacuated a crew member from a U.S. submarine off the coast of Greenland's capital, Nuuk, for urgent medical treatment. The timing raised questions about whether the submarine incident prompted the president's post.[1]

items.title: India postpones U.S. trade trip after Supreme Court strikes down Trump tariffs

featured_image.name: India delays Washington trade visit as U.S. policy shifts: source

items.description:
India has postponed a key trade delegation to Washington that was set to finalize an interim bilateral trade deal, after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump's sweeping tariff regime and the White House scrambled to replace it with new levies under an untested legal authority.

The Indian negotiating team, led by chief negotiator Darpan Jain, had been scheduled to begin a three-day meeting in Washington on February 23 to convert a framework agreement into a binding legal pact, according to Reuters. Both governments agreed the visit should be rescheduled after they assess the fallout from Friday's court ruling and Trump's rapid imposition of replacement tariffs.[1][2]

"The visit of the Indian chief negotiator and delegation will be scheduled later at a mutually convenient date once both governments complete internal assessments," a source familiar with the matter told CNBC. A new date has not been set, though sources indicated to India Today that the delay is expected to last weeks rather than months.[3][4]
